t: The Signature Tie System: Three Sizes, One Rule
title: The Signature Tie System: Three Sizes, One Rule
description: The Signature tie system stocks exactly three ties — 4-inch 18-lb white for thin wires, 8-inch 50-lb black for general bundles, 12-inch 75-lb black for trunks — and one rule: the bundle picks the smallest tie that fits with an inch of tail. No assortments of fourteen sizes, no guessing. Three sizes cover every PC job, and the rule keeps every tie tidy.

demo.program:
ties = [("4-in 18-lb white", "thin wires"), ("8-in 50-lb black", "general"),
        ("12-in 75-lb black", "trunks")]
for t, use in ties:
    print(f"  {t:<20} -> {use}")
print("Rule: smallest tie that fits + 1 in tail. Three sizes, every PC job.")

t: Signature Tension Standard: The Wiggle Test
title: Signature Tension Standard: The Wiggle Test
description: The Signature tension standard is the wiggle test: after cinching, grip the bundle and try to slide a cable — it should not move, but the jacket should show no dent when you press a fingernail into it. Apprentices practice on scrap cable until ten ties in a row pass. It takes an hour to learn and prevents a career of crushed insulation.

demo.program:
print("Wiggle test: cable must not slide; jacket must show no fingernail dent.")
print("Training: 10 ties in a row on scrap cable before touching a build.")
print("One hour of practice prevents a career of crushed insulation.")

title: Signature Flush-Cut Station
description: Every Signature bench has a flush-cut station: dedicated flush cutters on a magnetic holder, a small trash cup for tails, and a finger-test reminder card. Tails get cut at the station immediately after cinching — never 'later', because later never comes. The station makes the safe edge the default instead of a chore.

demo.program:
print("Station: flush cutters (magnetic holder) + tail trash cup + reminder card.")
print("Cut tails IMMEDIATELY after cinching. 'Later' never comes.")
print("The safe edge becomes the default, not a chore.")

title: Signature Permanent-Run Certification
description: Before a run gets zip ties, it must pass certification: is this bundle truly permanent? Will no upgrade touch it for the machine's life? If yes, it gets ties, a trunk card noting 'permanent — cut to change', and double-ties on heavy sections. If no, velcro. The certification stops the classic mistake: zip-tying something you will need to change next month.

demo.program:
print("Certify BEFORE tying: permanent for the machine's life?")
print("  YES -> ties + trunk card ('permanent - cut to change') + double-ties heavy")
print("  NO  -> velcro. No exceptions.")
print("Stops the classic mistake: tying what you'll change next month.")

title: Signature Releasable Bench Standard
description: Signature test benches use releasable ties exclusively — the tab-tab makes every bundle reworkable, and the bench's tie stock is 100 percent releasable so nobody grabs the wrong kind. Releasables cost more, but a bench that gets reconfigured weekly pays it back in not cutting and re-tying. Build kits stay single-use; benches stay releasable. The kinds never mix.

demo.program:
print("Test bench: 100% releasable ties (every bundle reworkable).")
print("Build kit: single-use ties. The kinds NEVER mix.")
print("Weekly-reconfigured bench pays back the releasable premium fast.")

title: Signature Mounting Grid for Desks
description: The Signature desk grid is a row of screw-mount tie heads along the desk's back edge on 6-inch centers — a permanent cable raceway. Power cables route through the left half, data through the right. New peripherals get tied into the grid in a minute. The grid turns 'under-desk cables' from a nest into infrastructure with addresses: everything has a position.

demo.program:
print("Desk grid: screw-mount heads every 6 in along back edge.")
print("Left half power, right half data. New peripheral: tied in, 1 minute.")
print("Every cable has an address: the nest becomes infrastructure.")

title: Signature vs Standard Tie Practice
description: Standard practice grabs whatever tie is handy, yanks it tight, and twists the tail off. Signature practice sizes the tie, wiggle-tests the tension, flush-cuts the tail at the station, and certifies permanence first. Same plastic, different discipline — and the difference shows the next time anyone reaches into the case.

demo.program:
print("Standard: any tie, yank tight, twist tail off.")
print("Signature: sized tie, wiggle-tested, flush-cut at station, permanence certified.")
print("Same plastic. Different discipline. Visible next time anyone reaches in.")

title: Signature Heavy-Trunk Specification
description: Signature spec for trunks over 1.25 inches diameter: double-ties every 6 inches, cross-tie at each end against axial slide, mounting-head anchors every 12 inches where possible. The spec is printed on the trunk card. Heavy trunks built to spec stay tight for the machine's life; heavy trunks built casually loosen within two years as nylon creeps.

demo.program:
print("Trunk >1.25 in: double-ties /6 in + cross-ties at ends + anchors /12 in.")
print("Spec printed on the trunk card. Casual heavy trunks loosen in ~2 years (creep).")
print("Spec'd trunks: tight for the machine's life.")

t: Signature Tail Discipline: Zero Sharp Edges
title: Signature Tail Discipline: Zero Sharp Edges
description: The Signature rule is zero sharp edges in any case a human will service: every tail flush-cut, finger-tested, and any scratch means re-cut. Apprentices learn that a sharp tail is a failed tie — not a cosmetic issue but a defect, because the next builder's bloody knuckle is the cost. Cases ship with the finger test passed, documented on the build card.

demo.program:
print("Rule: ZERO sharp edges in any serviced case.")
print("Every tail: flush-cut + finger-tested. Scratch = re-cut (it's a defect).")
print("Documented on the build card: finger test passed.")

title: Signature Color Protocol for Ties
description: Signature tie colors carry meaning: black for permanent hidden runs, white for thin-wire bundles, red for 'cut me first' service identification (the ties marking bundles that get serviced). A red tie in a case says 'this bundle opens for maintenance' — the next tech cuts red first and knows what to expect. Color turns ties into communication.

demo.program:
print("black: permanent hidden runs | white: thin-wire bundles | red: 'cut me first' service")
print("Red tie = this bundle opens for maintenance. Cut red first.")
print("Color turns ties into communication with the next tech.")

title: Signature Inspection Schedule
description: Signature maintenance inspects ties on a schedule: yearly flex tests on all visible ties, heat-zone ties checked every six months, and any tie near a replaced component gets replaced with it — new part, new ties. The schedule lives on the machine's service card. Ties are cheap; the labor of a failed tie letting cables hit a fan is not.

demo.program:
print("Yearly: flex-test all visible ties.")
print("6 months: heat-zone ties (near GPUs, radiators).")
print("With any part swap: new part, new ties.")
print("Logged on the machine's service card.")

title: Signature Beaded-Tie Test Kit
description: The Signature test-fit kit is a pouch of beaded releasable ties in three sizes — for mocking up routing before committing. Lay out the cable path with beaded ties, verify clearances and service loops, then replace with the final ties or velcro. Test fits stop being 'hold this while I look' and become a proper dry run.

demo.program:
print("Test-fit pouch: beaded ties, 3 sizes.")
print("Mock the routing -> verify clearances + loops -> commit final ties.")
print("'Hold this while I look' becomes a proper dry run.")

title: Signature Training: The Ten-Tie Drill
description: New builders drill ten ties on scrap cable: size it, cinch to wiggle-test, flush-cut, finger-test — ten in a row, timed. Under five minutes with zero defects passes. The drill builds the muscle memory that makes the discipline automatic under real build pressure, when nobody is watching the details.

demo.program:
print("Drill: 10 ties on scrap - size, cinch, wiggle-test, flush-cut, finger-test.")
print("Pass: under 5 minutes, zero defects.")
print("Builds muscle memory that holds up under real build pressure.")

title: Signature Outdoor and Heat-Zone Rules
description: Signature rules for hostile zones: UV-black ties only outdoors or near sunlit windows; stainless ties where exhaust heat exceeds nylon's comfort zone; releasables or velcro anywhere heat plus future service coincide. The zone gets noted on the trunk card so the next tech knows why the ties look different. Right tie, right zone, documented.

demo.program:
print("Outdoors/sunlit: UV-black only. Exhaust-heat zones: stainless.")
print("Heat + future service: releasables or velcro.")
print("Zone noted on trunk card: the next tech knows why ties look different.")
